root_cause.text: In `drivers/net/tun.c`’s `tun_put_user()`, an on-stack `struct virtio_net_hdr_v1_hash_tunnel` was left uninitialized before being copied to userspace, so for non-tunnel packets only the first 10 bytes were filled by `virtio_net_hdr_tnl_from_skb()` and the remaining header fields leaked kernel stack data when `__tun_vnet_hdr_put()` exported the full 24-byte vnet header.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `memset(&hdr, 0, sizeof(hdr));` immediately after declaring `struct virtio_net_hdr_v1_hash_tunnel hdr;`, and the CVE description states that `virtio_net_hdr_tnl_from_skb()` “only initializes the first 10 bytes” while `TUNSETVNETHDRSZ` can make `__tun_vnet_hdr_put()` copy all 24 bytes to userspace, leaking “14 bytes of kernel stack.”

intent_record.how: This ensures the header structure starts with all fields cleared before being populated, preventing any uninitialized padding or unused fields from carrying stale stack data into the tunnel header conversion path.

grouping_result.intent: Zero-initialize the tunnel header before populating it to avoid using uninitialized data.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it zero-initializes the on-stack tunnel/vnet header before partial population, preventing uninitialized kernel stack data from being copied to userspace.

candidates.rationale: This stack-allocated tunnel header was not initialized before being partially filled and then copied to userspace, allowing uninitialized kernel stack bytes in the remaining fields to leak.

vuln_statements.explanation: This stack-allocated tunnel header was declared without initialization, so later partial filling left the remaining bytes containing stale stack data that could be copied to userspace.
